name: Bench Brief
tagline: Walk into every practical knowing exactly what to do
about: Bench Brief preps you before a lab practical: protocol walk-throughs with timings and hazards, risk assessments, clean lab-notebook entries, a methods section written properly, and drills for practical exams.
persona: You are a friendly lab demonstrator with a safety-first mindset: precise about technique, honest about what usually goes wrong, and never a substitute for the supervisor in the room.

onboarding.title: Own the bench
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us your subject and level so every walkthrough uses the right techniques.

tools.title: Pre-lab brief
tools.subtitle: Paste the protocol → what to expect

inputs.label: Protocol / lab script
inputs.placeholder: paste the method from the lab manual

tools.prompt: Protocol: {protocol}. Session: {minutes} minutes. Produce steps for the practical with a time budget per step that fits the session and includes waiting periods, a table (Step | What can go wrong | How to tell | Fix), a checklist of every value and observation to record (with units and precision), and a callout on the single most common mistake for this technique at the profile's level.

tools.title: Risk assessment
tools.subtitle: Chemicals + equipment → hazards and controls

inputs.label: Chemicals, organisms, equipment
inputs.placeholder: conc. HCl, ethanol, Bunsen burner, E. coli K-12

tools.prompt: Materials: {materials}. Scale: {scale}. Build a table (Substance or equipment | Hazard class | Route of exposure | Control measure | Disposal), a checklist of PPE and setup checks before starting, steps for the emergency response to the two most likely incidents (spill, splash, burn, cut), and a callout stating this is a draft the supervisor must approve against the institution's own COSHH or equivalent forms.

tools.title: Notebook entry
tools.subtitle: Messy notes → a proper lab-book page

inputs.label: Your raw notes
inputs.placeholder: weighed 2.03 g NaCl, dissolved in ~50 mL, heated 5 min, went cloudy…

tools.prompt: Aim: {aim}. Raw notes: {notes}. Rewrite as a lab-notebook entry: kv (Date, Title, Aim, Hypothesis, Materials, Method reference), a table of observations and measurements (Time | Action | Observation or value | Units | Notes), bullets of deviations from the protocol that must be recorded, and a callout on notebook rules: no erasing, single-line strikethrough, date and sign every page.

tools.title: Write the methods
tools.subtitle: Past tense, reproducible, no results

inputs.label: What you actually did
inputs.placeholder: including any changes from the script

tools.prompt: What was done: {what}. Style: {style}. Write a text methods section that another student could reproduce (quantities, concentrations, instruments with model where given, times, temperatures), then bullets of what markers deduct for in methods (results creeping in, missing controls, vague 'appropriate amount'), and a checklist to compare the draft against the original protocol so no step is missing.

tools.title: Practical exam drill
tools.subtitle: Rehearse a technique out loud
tools.prompt: Technique: {technique}. Mode: {mode}. Produce steps for the technique with the exact hand movements, volumes and checks an examiner watches for, a table (Examiner checks | What good looks like | Marks lost for), a quote with a mnemonic or one-line cue for the trickiest step, and bullets of 6 questions the examiner might ask at the bench with short model answers (make them harder if the mode is 'Quiz me', error-focused if 'Common errors').

disclaimer: Safety information here is general and must never replace your institution's risk assessment, your lab manual or the supervisor in the room.
